The practical question is: “What can my child do now, what support will help next, and how will we understand progress?”

sections.text: COMPANY-DESCRIBED LEVELS OF DETAIL 17 domains. 79 abilities. 349 skills. A broad view of development, organised into abilities and skills that can inform a child-specific plan. The direction is practical: what helps this child communicate, learn, manage daily routines and take part in life? 17 Developmental domains The broad areas considered in Pinnacle’s framework. 79 Abilities The capabilities the framework helps organise. 349 Skills More detailed skills to connect with individual goals. 591 observations · AbilityScore® 0–1000 The company-described observation framework and score support a starting point and subsequent progress review. sections.text: Different starting points. Meaningful everyday goals. Families may arrive with questions about autism, ADHD, communication, sensory processing, movement, learning or other developmental concerns. Pinnacle’s stated purpose centres on the capabilities that help each child grow toward self-sufficiency and participate in mainstream life, with the support and accommodations they need. Communication and choice Express a need, make a choice and connect with other people. Daily-life independence Build participation in familiar routines and practise useful daily-living skills. Learning and belonging Take part in school, relationships and community with appropriate support. These are examples of individual goals, not promised results. Professional assessment identifies the support appropriate to each child; diagnosis and medical care remain important where indicated. The licensed software’s scope is non-diagnostic developmental support for ages 0–12, not treatment of every condition. sections.name: 01 Understand the child’s abilities
sections.description: AbilityScore® · 0–1000
sections.text: AbilityScore® · 0–1000 01 Understand the child’s abilities Begin with what the child can do, their interests and the everyday situations where support would help. Pinnacle describes 17 developmental domains, 79 abilities and 349 skills, supported by 591 observations and an AbilityScore on a 0–1000 scale. These are different layers of its developmental framework. For the family: A starting point the family and care team can discuss together. Company walkthrough, page 26; September handout, pages 5–6

sections.name: 06 Reassess and explain the trajectory

sections.text: Monthly AbilityScore refresh + progress review 06 Reassess and explain the trajectory Compare the child’s present abilities with their own earlier assessments and review the next priorities. The company walkthrough describes a monthly AbilityScore refresh; the Whitebook also describes monthly review. The care team should explain the schedule and any child-specific changes. sections.name: 07 Grow toward self-sufficiency and participation

sections.name: A population-scale ambition. One child’s life at the centre.
sections.description: Pinnacle describes a connected developmental-support architecture designed for wider deployment: a common framework, a persistent child-specific record, guided daily practice and human review. Its potential value at scale is continuity—helping families and professionals work from the same developmental direction across home, therapy and school.
sections.text: DESIGNED FOR WIDER REACH A population-scale ambition. One child’s life at the centre. Pinnacle describes a connected developmental-support architecture designed for wider deployment: a common framework, a persistent child-specific record, guided daily practice and human review. Its potential value at scale is continuity—helping families and professionals work from the same developmental direction across home, therapy and school. What makes “sovereign-ready” and “world-ready” meaningful? For a health system, sovereign readiness means demonstrable control over data and operations under its own governance requirements. International readiness also needs validated mappings, appropriate local language and workflows, applicable regulatory permissions, and evidence of safe, useful performance in that setting. Local control and accountability Document hosting location, data-controller responsibilities, lawful use, consent, access controls and audit trails. Interoperability in practice Validate the mappings and test information exchange with the systems that will actually use it. Capacity and real-world value Test deployment performance, accessibility and child-centred outcomes in the intended population and setting. The reviewed MD-5 and BIS scope establish specific regulatory and quality-system foundations. Reported network activity and information-security records add context. Together they support examining the deployment proposition; they are not a sovereign-grade certification or authorisation to operate in every country. How to interpret reported data volume The reported 2.7 billion+ structured records count database rows and events. They do not establish a nationally representative population, verified AI-training volume or population-level clinical effectiveness. sections.text: DESIGNED FOR WIDER REACH A population-scale ambition. One child’s life at the centre. Pinnacle describes a connected developmental-support architecture designed for wider deployment: a common framework, a persistent child-specific record, guided daily practice and human review. Its potential value at scale is continuity—helping families and professionals work from the same developmental direction across home, therapy and school. What makes “sovereign-ready” and “world-ready” meaningful? For a health system, sovereign readiness means demonstrable control over data and operations under its own governance requirements. International readiness also needs validated mappings, appropriate local language and workflows, applicable regulatory permissions, and evidence of safe, useful performance in that setting. Local control and accountability Document hosting location, data-controller responsibilities, lawful use, consent, access controls and audit trails. Interoperability in practice Validate the mappings and test information exchange with the systems that will actually use it. Capacity and real-world value Test deployment performance, accessibility and child-centred outcomes in the intended population and setting. The reviewed MD-5 and BIS scope establish specific regulatory and quality-system foundations. Reported network activity and information-security records add context. Together they support examining the deployment proposition; they are not a sovereign-grade certification or authorisation to operate in every country. How to interpret reported data volume The reported 2.7 billion+ structured records count database rows and events. They do not establish a nationally representative population, verified AI-training volume or population-level clinical effectiveness.
